О докторе Шахине Бастанинеджаде

Академический путь в Тегеране, Иран.

About Dr. Shahin Bastaninejad

Dr. Shahin Bastaninejad is a surgeon and specialist in ear, nose, and throat disease, with a focus on nasal plastic surgery.

He was born in 1978, is originally from Shiraz, and completed part of his education in Isfahan. He entered Isfahan University of Medical Sciences in 1996 and began residency in otolaryngology–head and neck surgery at Tehran University of Medical Sciences in 2005, graduating in 2009.

During residency he was recognized as an outstanding resident at Tehran University of Medical Sciences and ranked fourth in the national board examination. After completing service in Jahrom, Fars province (2009–2010), he joined the faculty at Amir Alam Hospital in Tehran.

He has published widely and has organized multiple courses in rhinoplasty and endoscopic sinus surgery. His clinical focus includes primary and secondary rhinoplasty, nasal reconstruction, nasal tumors, endoscopic sinus surgery, and skull-base collaboration with neurosurgery colleagues.

He is an Associate Professor of Otolaryngology at Tehran University of Medical Sciences and a member of the scientific committee of the Iranian Rhinology and Facial Plastic Association. He has also held leadership roles in education and clinic management at Amir Alam Hospital.

pages.content_html:
После снятия шины

Соблюдайте письменный план хирурга.

Important points after splint removal

After the external splint is removed, swelling and sensitivity can continue for weeks. Protect the nose from trauma, avoid heavy glasses if advised, and keep follow-up visits.

Do not manipulate tapes or sutures. Use only rinses, ointments, or medications approved by your care team. Sleep position and activity limits should follow your written instructions—not generic internet advice.

Contact the clinic promptly for heavy bleeding, fever, severe pain, or sudden breathing difficulty.

faqs.question: What are clinic hours and the last admission time?
faqs.answer_html: Saturday to Tuesday, 15:00–18:00. Patients who arrive after 18:00 will not be admitted under any circumstances.

faqs.question: What is the acceptable age range for surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Eligible age is 18–45 years. Cases outside this range are reviewed only with the surgeon’s explicit approval.

faqs.question: How long after a previous surgery can revision be considered?
faqs.answer_html: At least 24 months should have passed since the prior operation, unless the surgical team defines a different plan for your case.

faqs.question: How do I book a consultation?
faqs.answer_html: Use the online booking form on the website or contact the clinic by phone. After submission, the reception team coordinates the appointment.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the visit?
faqs.answer_html: Bring identification, prior imaging or operative notes if any, a list of medications, and any previous before/after photos requested by the team.

faqs.question: Which medicines should be stopped before surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Follow only the written instructions from your surgical team. Do not start or stop any drug, supplement, or herbal product on your own.

faqs.question: Is smoking or vaping allowed before surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Smoking and nicotine products impair healing. Stop them for the period your surgeon specifies before and after surgery.

faqs.question: How should I fast before surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Follow the exact fasting instructions given for your admission time. Do not eat or drink outside that plan.

faqs.question: What general care is needed in the first days?
faqs.answer_html: Follow the care plan from your team: reduce salt, drink enough water, avoid heavy bending and strenuous activity, and take medications exactly as prescribed.

faqs.question: How should sutures be cared for?
faqs.answer_html: Keep sutures clean, do not manipulate them, and avoid pressure, trauma, or excessive upper-lip stretching. Use repair creams only if approved by the care team.

faqs.question: When can I shower after surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Usually after 72 hours, with a short shower as directed. The cast and tapes must not get wet or shift, and water should not be very hot.

faqs.question: What should I eat in the first days?
faqs.answer_html: Choose light, soft, low-salt foods. Avoid hard, spicy, or salty items that need heavy chewing. See the clinic’s anti-inflammatory diet article for nutrition guidance.

faqs.question: Are milk, yogurt, and other dairy allowed on the anti-inflammatory diet?
faqs.answer_html: No. All dairy is restricted; cottage cheese is the only approved exception within the planned amount because of its protein content.

faqs.question: Are mashed potatoes or tomatoes recommended after surgery?
faqs.answer_html: No. Potato, mashed potato, and tomato are considered inflammatory in this protocol and are not allowed.

faqs.question: Is rice or rice pudding allowed on the anti-inflammatory diet?
faqs.answer_html: No. Rice, rice pudding, and rice-based products are not allowed in this protocol.

faqs.question: How long does the anti-inflammatory diet continue?
faqs.answer_html: At least one month after surgery, unless your care team sets a different plan for your case.

faqs.question: When should post-op medications start?
faqs.answer_html: Start medications after discharge exactly as prescribed. Do not change, stop, or add sprays, rinses, or ointments on your own.

faqs.question: How long does the splint stay on the nose?
faqs.answer_html: Usually about one week; exact timing depends on your nose and the surgeon’s judgment. The splint must not get wet, loosen, or shift.

faqs.question: Is blood-tinged discharge or congestion normal?
faqs.answer_html: Light blood-tinged discharge in the first 24–72 hours and mild congestion can be normal. Report heavy or ongoing bleeding, fever, uncontrolled pain, or significant breathing difficulty to the care team immediately.

faqs.question: How should I sleep and rest after surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Follow only the instructions given for your case. Do not rely on generic internet advice or outdated posts.

faqs.question: Is internal nasal packing used?
faqs.answer_html: Under the clinic’s current approach, internal mesh or packing is usually not used; the final decision depends on the operative findings.

faqs.question: How many days will I stay in hospital after surgery?
faqs.answer_html: Discharge timing depends on your condition and the care team’s assessment; you will be reviewed before leaving.
